title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. I is a 3-element set (I ∈ Ob Ens_3), and S0 T_{0,I} is Grothendieck's discrete model of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid with |I| = 3 boundary components (the 'pair of pants' level of the Teichmüller tower). Its object set is or(I), the two cyclic orientations of I, which is a μ2-torsor. The previous page sets up the canonical extension (S) 0→Z→R→U→0, the universal cover of the circle U. Its I-th power gives (S_I) of U^I by Z^I. The automorphism groupoid is described by pulling (S_I) back along μ2 →diag μ2^I ⊂ U^I.

Step 1. Restricted to μ2 = {±1} ⊂ U, (S) becomes the standard extension (K_1): 0→Z →2 Z→Z/2→0, since the preimage of {±1} in R is (1/2)Z, rescaled.

Step 2. Taking the I-th power and pulling back along the diagonal gives (13). This page rewrites (13) as the pushout (15) of (K_1) along the diagonal Z→Z^I. Concretely the middle group is E_I = {n ∈ Z^I : all n_i have the same parity} = (2Z)^I + Z·(1,…,1). It sits in 0 → Z^I (embedded as (2Z)^I) → E_I → μ2 → 0. Its class in Ext(Z/2, Z^I) = (Z/2)^I is the diagonal element, which is nonzero, so the extension is non-split.

Step 3. Hence for any μ2-torsor ε (a 2-element set) one gets a groupoid on ε. For x, y ∈ ε, Hom(x,y) is the Z^I-torsor T_{x−y} ∧_Z Z^I, where T_{x−y} is the fibre of Z→Z/2 over x−y. This torsor is Z^I (really (2Z)^I, rescaled) if x = y, and Imp^I (I-tuples of odd integers) if x ≠ y. Composition is addition.

Step 4. Take ε = or(I). This gives a complete algebraic description of S0 T_{0,I}, functorial in I and so compatible with the action of S_I. Geometrically, the generator 2 ∈ 2Z is the full Dehn twist about a boundary component. An odd vector (1,1,1) is the simultaneous half-twist at the three boundaries, which exchanges the two hexagons ('front/back') of the pants, i.e. reverses the cyclic orientation. Equivalently, on P^1 with tangent vectors at 0, 1, ∞, the involution z↦1−z negates all three tangent vectors, so it must be followed by a half-rotation at each point.

Step 5 (next page). The resulting S_I-equivariant fundamental group is π1(S0T_{0,I}, S_I; x) = {(α, n) ∈ S_I × Z^I : n ∈ E_I with parity of the n_i equal to sgn(α)}, with (l,α)(l',α') = (l + α(l'), αα'). This is the extension of S_I by Z^I obtained from the semidirect product E_I ⋊ S_I by pulling back along the signature S_I → Z/2. Equivalently, it is the orbifold fundamental group of the moduli stack of (P^1, 3 marked points, nonzero tangent vectors)/S_3, i.e. of [(C^*)^3/S_3].
errors: No mathematical error. Notational point only: in (16), 'Hom(x,x) ≃ Z^I' tacitly identifies (2Z)^I with Z^I via division by 2. The torsor Imp^I is naturally a (2Z)^I-torsor, so with the literal identification the two cases sit in the ambient Z^I with different normalisations. The consistent reading is E_I ⊂ Z^I as described.
The torsor T_{x−y} is a torsor under Z acting via multiplication by 2. This is implicit in writing T_{x−y} ∧_Z Z^I.

ideas.what: Pushout of the extension Z →2 Z → Z/2 along the diagonal Z→Z^I, giving the non-split extension E_I of μ2 by Z^I (vectors of constant parity)
ideas.modern_name: Pushout / Baer functoriality of extensions; class = diagonal element of Ext^1(Z/2, Z^I)

ideas.what: Description of the genus-0, 3-holed Teichmüller groupoid as a groupoid on the two cyclic orientations of I, with Hom-sets Z^I (Dehn twists) or Imp^I (simultaneous half-twists swapping the two hexagons)
ideas.modern_name: Discrete Teichmüller (Lego) groupoid at level (0,3); tangential base points with half-twists/braiding
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984, in outline); made explicit by Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Funar–Gelca
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the first two levels of the Teichmüller tower, but not this explicit torsor description as far as known

ideas.what: S_I-equivariant π1 as the extension of S_I by Z^I pulled back from E_I ⋊ S_I via the signature (odd permutations lift with all-odd twist vectors)
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of the moduli stack of 3-pointed P^1 with tangent vectors, modulo S_3; related to the framed/ribbon braid relation (braiding squared = twists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in GT/Teichmüller tower literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov)

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is correct, clean and explicit. The torsor-theoretic description of S0 T_{0,3} via orientations and odd/even twist vectors, with the extension of S_3 controlled by the signature, is a nice unpublished detail of Grothendieck's Teichmüller-groupoid programme. Its content is nevertheless the well-known level-(0,3) structure: half-twists, braiding squared equals Dehn twists, and the orbifold π1 of [(C^*)^3/S_3]. This structure is standard in the later Lego–Teichmüller/GT literature.
transcription_corrections: Diagram (15): the vertical arrows are the diagonal maps and the right arrow is an isomorphism Z/2Z ≅ μ2. The bottom row is 0 → Z^I → E_I → μ2 → 0.
Line 'ou tenseurs de I ∈ Ob Ens_3' more plausibly reads 'en termes de I ∈ Ob Ens_3' (or 'pour I ∈ Ob Ens_3'); 'tenseurs' is likely a misreading.
'ε = or(I)' (orientations of I) is confirmed. On the previous and next pages, 'ω(I)' is probably the same symbol or(I).
In (16) the side note reads 'si x ≠ y, où Imp est l'ens. des entiers impairs'. The case x = y gives Z^I.
Last line: 'Cette description est compatible avec les opérations de 𝔖_I. On trouvera donc une [description des groupes fondamentaux…]'.
